# Brali

> A practical knowledge library for people, developers, researchers, and AI agents.

Brali publishes atomic practical hacks, executable protocols, a practical knowledge ontology, evidence states, evidence decisions, research candidates, and machine-readable contracts. The original Brali LifeOS app is still available, but the knowledge library and data are now the main project.

## Knowledge model v2

- Domain: broad area of practical life or work.
- Topic: concrete problem, capability, or outcome.
- Method: named structured approach that may cross Topics and Domains.
- Lens: transferable way of thinking borrowed from a discipline, profession, philosophy, or strategic tradition. A Lens is not evidence.
- Hack: the smallest reusable practical technique.
- Protocol: an executable sequence or personal experiment that can reference one or more hacks.
- Evidence state: `reviewed`, `practical`, `pending-review`, or `restricted`.
- Research candidate: discovery metadata. It is not evidence, even when its workflow status changes after review.
- Evidence decision: explicit source-review record describing what a source supports, what it does not support, limitations, and the editorial decision.

Recommended classification stack: `Domain -> Topic -> Hack -> Protocol`, with optional Method and Lens tags and separate Evidence/source provenance.

Legacy `Life Area` and `Growth Zone` fields and URLs are preserved for compatibility. A legacy Growth Zone may map to a Topic, Method, or Lens through the ontology. Do not assume every Growth Zone is a Topic.

`topic-pending` is an intentional migration state. It means a legacy Method or Lens collection identifies a useful secondary classification but the concrete Topic for that individual record still requires editorial classification.

Research promotion path: `research candidate -> evidence decision -> hack -> protocol -> ontology -> publish`.

## Machine-readable data

- Knowledge ontology: https://brali-lifeos.github.io/life-os/datasets/ontology.json
- Ontology coverage: https://brali-lifeos.github.io/life-os/datasets/ontology-coverage.json
- Trusted Protocol Feed: https://brali-lifeos.github.io/life-os/datasets/protocols.json
- Full library corpus: https://brali-lifeos.github.io/life-os/datasets/hacks.json
- Evidence index: https://brali-lifeos.github.io/life-os/datasets/evidence.json
- Evidence decisions: https://brali-lifeos.github.io/life-os/datasets/evidence-decisions.json
- Existing content review queue: https://brali-lifeos.github.io/life-os/datasets/review-queue.json
- Research search lenses: https://brali-lifeos.github.io/data/research-queries.json
- Research candidate queue: https://brali-lifeos.github.io/data/research-candidates.json
- Agent registry: https://brali-lifeos.github.io/agents/registry.json

Trusted Protocol Feed schema v3 and Evidence Index schema v2 expose an `ontology` object with Domains, Topics, Methods, Lenses, classification status, and legacy compatibility identifiers. New integrations should use this object rather than treating `life_area` or `growth_zone` as the canonical semantic model.

Use `evidence-decisions.json` as the audit trail between a research candidate and a public content change. A decision records the actual source reviewed, the supported claim, unsupported/overstated claims, limitations, and whether the candidate is rejected, watched, used to support/challenge existing content, or allowed to propose a Hack/Protocol. A `watch` decision is deliberately not a recommendation.

Research query and candidate schema v2 records use canonical `domain_ids`, `topic_ids`, `method_ids`, and `lens_ids`. Legacy Life Area and Growth Zone fields remain during migration.

## Contracts

- Hack: https://brali-lifeos.github.io/contracts/hack.schema.json
- Protocol: https://brali-lifeos.github.io/contracts/protocol.schema.json
- Research Candidate: https://brali-lifeos.github.io/contracts/research-candidate.schema.json
- Evidence Decision: https://brali-lifeos.github.io/contracts/evidence-decision.schema.json

Hack and Protocol contracts support `domain_slugs`, `topic_slugs`, `method_slugs`, and `lens_slugs`. Legacy `life_area_slugs` and `zone_slugs` remain during migration for older consumers.

## Agent skills

- Research Discovery: https://brali-lifeos.github.io/skills/research-discovery/SKILL.md
- Evidence Review: https://brali-lifeos.github.io/skills/evidence-review/SKILL.md
- Protocol Design: https://brali-lifeos.github.io/skills/protocol-design/SKILL.md
- Taxonomy Curation: https://brali-lifeos.github.io/skills/taxonomy-curation/SKILL.md

For normal recommendation or retrieval, start with the Trusted Protocol Feed and use the ontology to match the user's concrete Topic. For research/maintenance work, inspect the candidate, its Evidence Decision if one exists, and the direct source before changing content. Never promote a candidate from search metadata directly into `reviewed` content, and never convert `watch` into a recommendation merely because a source looks relevant.

Only `reviewed` and `practical` entries enter the Trusted Protocol Feed. English is the main published language today. The public interface today is the static dataset/contract layer; a future MCP service may add tools over the same records. The current public license is non-commercial; commercial use requires a separate agreement.
